Uncloud v0.4.37 updates Windows x64, macOS Apple Silicon and Linux x64 from the same source. All three installers and the signed updater files are published together.

- Model loading now prepares the native MLX runtime and tokenizer before reporting ready. Native context checks and Chisel planning reuse the engine connection. Fresh first-response tests used new prompts with zero reused prefix tokens; no saved answers were served. This reduces initial preparation delays, but does not establish a sustained generation-speed increase.
- Models now includes a Benchmark section with first-token timing, generation rate and token usage. Loaded models shows the native allocated context and cache information. Compatible native prompt caches reuse computation for conversation prefixes; every answer is still generated by the model.
- Context counting continues to use the complete native template, tools and retained evidence. Hybrid model metadata no longer receives an inappropriate dense-cache estimate. Custom context changes reload the selected model; Auto remains bounded by runtime capabilities and available memory. Rolling summaries and conversation recall retain original saved messages but remain lossy and relevance-dependent.
- Native tool exposure uses compact schemas and call syntax. Ordinary Chat adds no model identity correction, date or persona instruction. Chisel retains its coding tools. Optional Personas includes six editable fictional styles; none is enabled automatically in Chat or Chisel. Tool availability does not guarantee reliable model self-identification.
- Chat can render validated bar-chart data directly from a native chart tool call. Numeric tables also offer a chart view. Rendering does not execute model-generated Python or web code. Tool selection and factual values remain the model's responsibility; a Python plotting reply can still remain code.
- Chat exposes attachments for supported text files and image formats when the running model reports vision support. Message widths and hover actions are aligned, and generation status appears above the input. PDF extraction is not supported.
- Public web search tries an additional DuckDuckGo layout before falling back. Failed native lookups return structured errors so the model can refine its query within the existing bounded limit. Results retain source URLs; provider challenges, unrelated results and availability can still prevent a lookup.
- First-run deployment reports known package download sizes, package count, estimated free-space reserve and destination free space. Python, models and optional runtimes can require additional downloads. Preflight and engine-deployment wording stays in the UI and is not sent to ordinary Chat.

Validation before packaging: the clean release snapshot passed 1,141 backend tests (12 optional tests skipped). All 223 frontend tests passed, and the frontend production build and macOS application build passed. GitHub additionally checks source tests and packages each operating system. Live inference tests ran sequentially on one Apple Silicon Mac; Windows GPU behavior, Linux inference and clean first-run download totals were not verified on physical target machines.

Performance depends on the device and power profile. The same current Qwen3.5 9B runtime measured about 27 generated tokens/second on AC, 13.6 on battery with Low Power Mode enabled, and 25 after reconnecting, with zero reused prompt tokens and no engine or model changes between those requests. Older and current source also both measured about 26.7 on AC. This release improves initial response preparation; it does not guarantee those rates on other devices or resolve every model's thinking loop.
